title: Inside ELWAY’s 2026 NFL forecast
contentHtml:
No, I’m not sure why the NFL is starting its season on a Wednesday. But I won’t complain because it should be a hell of a lot more fun than watching the Republican midterm convention. The NFL is back tonight with a Super Bowl rematch between the Patriots and Seahawks, and then the Rams will play the 49ers tomorrow night U.S. time in Melbourne, Australia.

Over the weekend, we relaunched our NFL model, ELWAY, and our quarterback rating system, QBERT. ELWAY made some smart calls last year — it was bullish on the Seahawks and the Pats, for instance — but also had its share of misses, clinging to hope for the Chiefs, Lions and Ravens until it was far too late. Never satisfied, we’ve made quite a few improvements to ELWAY and QBERT this year and also upgraded our charts and visual presentation.

Since ELWAY is still a relatively new system, I thought it would be better to show you the season through the model’s eyes, rather than giving you some sort of traditional, 32-team X’s-and-O’s preview. Therefore, we’re officially dubbing this a rare sports Model Talk.

So see the ELWAY landing page for our final, extremely detailed preseason forecast.1 This newsletter is intended as a complement, a hybrid between a season preview and an explainer. But a lot of this should interest even medium-nerdy football fans. For example, we have a fun way to account for strength of schedule by scrambling the positions of all 32 teams in each simulation. Here’s what we’ll cover:

  • How ELWAY compares to Vegas;

  • Which teams are helped and hurt the most by the schedule;

  • The impact of injuries;

  • Roster ratings versus performance ratings and how ELWAY combines them;

  • Finally, the impact of quarterbacks, who are especially important in ELWAY because of QBERT.

How ELWAY compares to Vegas

A projection model will never solve the problem that a 17-game NFL season with imbalanced schedules is inherently going to introduce a degree of randomness. Indeed, the degree of parity in the league this year might be higher than in most seasons. The best teams in 2025 had little correlation with the elite sides of 2024: the Patriots were 4-13 two years ago. Few teams are on a sustainable, multi-year dynastic streak like we used to see with Brady’s Patriots or the Peak Mahomes Chiefs.

Moreover, this is a weird era for quarterbacks. Josh Allen is probably the best QB in the sport, but he’s coming off his lowest passing yardage total since 2019. Lamar Jackson’s year was a lost cause. Matthew Stafford is 38. Drake Maye has an argument for being the most valuable long-term asset in the league, but the adjustments we made to QBERT this summer — and his middling performance in the playoffs — hurt him. Mahomes has a chance for a remarkable recovery, but he’s coming off an ACL/MCL tear.

Still, one thing that helps when working on a sports model is that you can use Vegas odds2 as a sanity check. That doesn’t mean Vegas is necessarily right, and we think ELWAY has a few insights that typical sports bettors might lack, like about the importance of injuries. Moreover, it would be boring if models perfectly aligned with Vegas on every game. But if your model shows profound, systematic differences from Vegas, it’s probably doing something wrong.

Disclaimer

We think ELWAY is a really cool model. But before we go behind the paywall, keep in mind that NFL betting lines are notoriously tough to beat. We wouldn’t necessarily expect ELWAY alone to be enough. Late-breaking injuries and weather can also materially affect betting lines after ELWAY posts its weekly update. ELWAY + football knowledge + some betting street smarts might bring you closer. But we’re mostly using this as a diagnostic exercise. The differences between ELWAY and Vegas can reveal how the model “thinks” about football.
